A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Temporal Sparse Autoencoder work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and newly added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original Pythia-160m and Gemma2-2b experiments, probing and reconstruction results, ablations, steering experiments, and HH-RLHF data analysis in Section 4 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds smoothness diagnostics, absorption measurements, baseline activation comparisons, and a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct scaling study in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The feature partition, Matryoshka reconstruction objective, symmetric temporal contrastive loss, and paired-token training procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A's linearized loss is presented as future work, not as a replacement used by the reported method.

E1.justification: The documented coverage retains the Pile, MMLU, Wikipedia, FineFineWeb, HH-RLHF, and the same spliced passages. New smoothness and absorption checks assess representation properties without documenting a distinct data domain or input scenario. The Llama study changes model configuration within the existing MMLU evaluation.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 8 adds Matryoshka, BatchTopK, and Neuronpedia Matryoshka comparisons for the four-passage sequence shown only with T-SAE features in v1 Figure 4. The comparator sets in the original benchmark, probing, and steering experiments are retained.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation with Fourier, wavelet, and multiscale smoothness procedures, SAEBench absorption evaluation, and a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct experiment using a reported 20% training-step budget. The original Pythia/Gemma settings remain. Specifying the last 20 tokens for the existing visualization is additional documentation, rather than evidence of a changed experiment.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds complementary smoothness analyses, matched baseline traces for the spliced-text case study, an absorption diagnostic, and a larger-model scaling analysis. Appendix D adds an audit of public SAE features associated with 'the'. The original feature-split, random-contrast, and noncontrastive ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Autointerpretability standard deviations, the HH-RLHF two-sided t-test, and correlation significance reporting are retained. The new absorption table extends the existing mean-plus-spread reporting style to additional outcomes. No new seed information, repeated-run protocol, confidence-interval procedure, or significance-testing method is specified.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results in Tables 9–10 and Figures 8–9, including frequency-based smoothness scores, absorption outcomes, baseline activation traces, and qualitative Llama scaling findings. For example, Table 10 reports mean absorption fractions of 0.24±0.16 for T-SAE and 0.22±0.16 for Matryoshka. Original core benchmark, probing, ablation, and steering results are retained; the split smoothness values added to Table 1 already appeared in v1 Table 4.

T1.justification: Assumption 2 removes the additive decomposition g(h,l)=g_H(h)+g_L(l) and stated residual orthogonality, replacing them with a weaker reconstruction bound involving g(h,0). New Appendix A derives a candidate linearized contrastive objective. This materially expands the mathematical content, although the derivation contains errors, including retaining exp(s_ii) after taking its logarithm.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain temporal-prior-based feature disentanglement, improved semantic/contextual recovery without substantial reconstruction cost, and practical dataset-understanding and steering benefits. The shorter abstract and revised contribution wording do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of collapse prevention and selective control through feature specialization. Appendix A newly discusses paired-token memory costs, the single-hierarchy limitation, and the implications of nonnegative feature geometry. Appendix C.3 also adds an absorption interpretation, but its claim of fewer split features conflicts with Table 10's 2.19 for T-SAE versus 1.96 for Matryoshka.

D1.justification: v2 specifies that the existing visualization uses the last 20 tokens and documents new diagnostic recipes, including the Fourier frequency split, three wavelet iterations, and an eight-token moving window. It also discloses the scaling study's relative training budget. Existing hyperparameters, steering instructions, and code/model release information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted connections to temporal-supervision SAEs, including Menon et al. and Li and Ren, and to temporal representation learning through Oord, Hyvarinen and Morioka, and Klindt. It relates preference-data analysis to Movva et al. and removes some earlier background citations. The overall linguistic-prior positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and dataset case-study exposition are condensed, several explanations and captions are revised, and author/header information and citation style change. The appendices are reorganized, with the former additional-results Appendix A becoming Appendix C. The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The ICLR template substantially changes margins, headers, author layout, and figure sizing. Table 1 incorporates the earlier appendix smoothness table; the steering examples move from main-text Table 2 to appendix Table 7. New baseline-comparison and scaling figures and expanded diagnostic tables materially extend the visual presentation, beyond renumbering and relocation.

improvement.justification: The added smoothness diagnostics, matched spliced-text baseline comparisons, and explicit resource limitations make the unchanged central method better supported and easier to assess. The gain is limited: scaling evidence is qualitative and uses a partial training budget, while Appendix A introduces algebraic errors and Appendix C.3 misinterprets the split-feature counts in Table 10. These problems affect ancillary additions rather than the retained main experiments, leaving a modest net improvement.
